$comment: Cross-language verdict-parity fixtures (C4). Each language implements the named net builders in its own test code (per the cross-lang-dot-parity.sh pattern: shared expectations, per-language builders) and asserts the expected verdict with certificate checking ON. netDescription is the normative builder contract. The optional `sinkPlaces` array names places to declare as expected terminal places on the verifier (VER-002 sink semantics: a quiescent marking is a deadlock violation only when NO declared sink holds a token); omit it for closed nets. A language disagreeing with `expected` is a parity FINDING to report, never to paper over. The optional `route` marker (`"B"`) declares that the fixture is decided by the ν name-aware state-class-graph verifier (NU-050 Route B), NOT by the SMT/flat or coloured encoders (Route A): every runner MUST assert the verifier report names Route B BEFORE comparing the verdict, so a fixture that silently falls back to Route A fails loudly instead of passing vacuously, and MUST skip the violated-counterexample-replay strengthening (Route B reports counterexampleConfirmed = null by construction — its trace is a path of the name-partition graph, not of the flat abstract semantics). Route B needs no `budgetPlaces` knob for these fixtures and MUST NOT be given one: the Route B trigger for a quiescence property is `has-match-spec` alone (a declared budget only matters for reachability-safety), and declaring a budget would additionally enable the NU-053 defer-to-Route-A path on truncation — which is exactly the silent Route A fallback these fixtures exist to catch. Fixtures carrying `route: "B"` pin a KNOWN cross-route disagreement on the deadlock predicate (see their netDescription); they are documentation of that divergence and neither route's predicate may be edited to make them agree.

fixtures.netDescription: Places p0(1 token),p1,p2; t01: one(p0)->p1; t12: one(p1)->p2; t20: one(p2)->p0. The token circulates forever.

Places p0(1 token),p1,p2; t01: one(p0)->p1; t12: one(p1)->p2. After t12 fires nothing is enabled. p2 must be a consumed-from place nowhere, i.e. a genuine dead marking (declare p2 as a normal place, not a declared sink, so quiescence counts as deadlock per each verifier's established deadlock fixture).
Places idle1(1),idle2(1),lock(1),crit1,crit2; enter1: one(idle1)+one(lock)->crit1; exit1: one(crit1)->idle1+lock; enter2/exit2 symmetric. Binary semaphore guarantees exclusion.
Same as mutexLocked but enter1/enter2 do NOT consume lock (lock place omitted entirely). Both criticals reachable simultaneously.
Places p0(3 tokens),p1; t: one(p0)->p1. Conservation p0+p1=3. This certificate needs the P-invariant strengthening, exercising the R'-candidate certificate check.
Environment place e (always-available/unbounded injection mode per VER-006), t: one(e)->p1. Injection makes p1 exceed any bound.
Places p0(1),blocker(1),p1; t: one(p0), inhibitor(blocker) -> p1. Nothing ever drains blocker, so t never fires and p1 stays empty.

The Strengthening.lean H1 witness: t: all(p0)->p1 with p0(2 tokens). The y=(1,1) invariant must be dropped by the H1 guard (report carries the H1 reason) and the bound genuinely violated (p1 reaches 1).

Places p0(3 tokens),p1; t: atLeast(2)(p0)->p1 producing ONE token to p1. AtLeast drains all available (>=2), so t fires at most once from M0 and p1 <= 1. Its invariant is H1-dropped; the proof must come from the encoder's consume-all arm alone.

Places p0(1 token),done,stuck; ONE transition t: one(p0) -> AND(out(done), out(stuck)) producing one token into each. `done` is declared a sink via this fixture's sinkPlaces. The only quiescent marking is {done:1, stuck:1} - it holds a token in the declared sink AND one in the non-sink `stuck`. Per VER-002 the deadlock error condition is (all transitions disabled) AND (no sink place has a token), so the token resting in `done` excuses the quiescent marking even though `stuck` is also marked.

Places p0(1 token) and done (starts empty, declared a sink via this fixture's sinkPlaces); ONE transition t: one(p0) with NO output spec - a sink transition carrying the passthrough action, permitted by CORE-042 (CORE-043 AC4). `done` touches no arc, so it must be declared explicitly on the net builder (place()/places()) or it will not exist in the flattened net. After t fires the net holds no tokens anywhere: every transition is disabled and no sink place has a token, which is exactly VER-002's error condition.

ν net (name minting → matched join), decided by Route B. Places source(1 token), branchA, branchB, done, stuck; branchA/branchB are the ν-join's correlated inputs, hence the fragment's COLOURED places, and so must start empty. fork: one(source) -> AND(out(branchA), out(branchB)) — one firing co-mints ONE fresh name into both branches. join: one(branchA) + one(branchB) correlated by NameId equality on the token payload -> AND(out(done), out(stuck)); it produces only into ordinary places, so the net stays inside the BASE mint→matched-join fragment. `done` is declared a sink via this fixture's sinkPlaces; `stuck` is deliberately NOT. The net has exactly one quiescent marking: fork is enabled only at M0, join is enabled only at {branchA:1, branchB:1} and its correlation succeeds because both tokens carry the same co-minted name, and the resulting {done:1, stuck:1} enables nothing — so Route B's `quiescent AND NOT(every marked place is a declared sink)` holds (`stuck` is marked and is not a sink) and the answer is violated. Non-vacuity: a violated here would ALSO be reachable the wrong way, by the ν correlation failing and the net quiescing at {branchA:1, branchB:1} (neither branch is a sink), so the standing guard is the sibling fixture nu-drained-terminal-route-b-proven, which is built on the identical fork/join correlation and would turn violated for exactly that reason — the pair only passes together when the co-minted name really does correlate. Route A implements spec/07-verification.md VER-002 verbatim — `quiescent AND (no declared sink place holds a token)` — and therefore answers PROVEN on this very marking shape (see the sibling fixture sink-partial-terminal-proven, which pins Route A on {done:1, stuck:1}), so the two routes genuinely disagree here and this fixture records that disagreement deliberately, pending a semantics decision on which predicate VER-002 should mandate; until that decision lands, neither predicate may be edited to make the pair agree (spec/12-nu-nets.md NU-053 AC3).

ν net (name minting → matched join), decided by Route B. Places source(1 token), branchA, branchB and done; branchA/branchB are the ν-join's correlated inputs, hence COLOURED, and so must start empty. fork: one(source) -> AND(out(branchA), out(branchB)) — one firing co-mints ONE fresh name into both branches. join: one(branchA) + one(branchB) correlated by NameId equality, with NO output spec — a sink transition carrying the structure-only/passthrough action, permitted by CORE-042 (CORE-043 AC4); producing nothing keeps it inside the BASE fragment. `done` starts empty, is declared a sink via this fixture's sinkPlaces, and touches NO arc, so it MUST be declared explicitly on the net builder (place()/places()) — the same requirement the Route A sibling carries, and what makes the sink declaration resolve against the flattened net rather than naming a place that is not there. Note the honest scope of that: Route B's predicate quantifies over the MARKED places only, and the witness marking here is empty, so Route B answers proven whether or not `done` resolves — the declaration is what makes this fixture MEAN what it says (and keeps it structurally identical to its Route A sibling apart from the ν layer), not what makes it pass. The real vacuity risk for a Route B fixture is a silent fall-back to Route A, which the `route` marker guards. The net has exactly one quiescent marking, the empty one: fork is enabled only at M0, join is enabled only at {branchA:1, branchB:1} and consumes the matched pair without producing anything, after which the net holds no tokens anywhere — so Route B's `quiescent AND NOT(every marked place is a declared sink)` is FALSE (vacuously, there is no marked place outside the sinks) and the answer is proven. That proven is NOT vacuous: it is reachable only if the ν join actually correlates the co-minted pair and drains it; were the correlation to fail the net would quiesce at {branchA:1, branchB:1}, neither branch is a sink, and this fixture would turn violated. Route A implements spec/07-verification.md VER-002 verbatim — `quiescent AND (no declared sink place holds a token)` — and therefore answers VIOLATED on this very marking shape (see the sibling fixture sink-drained-terminal-violated, which pins Route A on the empty terminal marking), so the two routes genuinely disagree here and this fixture records that disagreement deliberately, pending a semantics decision on which predicate VER-002 should mandate; until that decision lands, neither predicate may be edited to make the pair agree (spec/12-nu-nets.md NU-053 AC3).
